resources.string: TLS inspection (Sensitive Advanced)
Selected-app HTTP-over-TLS inspection runs only during the active local VPN. Plaintext stays in bounded memory and is never sent to the remote stream.
Show TLS-inspection setup
Off by default. Nothing creates a certificate or opens Android Settings until you explicitly continue.
Inspection is ready only after CA setup, trust verification, consent, and app selection
The active route is bounded to selected-app HTTP over TLS 1.2/1.3 when the provider supports the offered version. It is not universal HTTPS inspection.
Certificate pinning is not bypassed. QUIC and non-HTTP TLS are rejected; credentials and bodies are transient only, with no automatic export or remote sharing.
At most 25 explicitly selected, known non-sensitive apps are eligible. Banking, payments, authentication, password-manager, health, shared-UID, and uncertain apps are mandatory exclusions.
Select only eligible apps. Shared-UID, banking, payment, authentication, password-manager, health, and uncertain packages stay excluded. Unknown attribution is never intercepted.

The selected-app policy is bounded to 25 packages. Shared-UID, banking, payment, authentication, password-manager, health, and uncertain packages are always rejected. Unknown flow attribution bypasses interception.
Known package rows shown: %1$d. Selected: %2$d of 25.
%1$s — this package is unclassified or shared, so it is excluded by mandatory policy.
Separate inspection-session acknowledgement
This acknowledgement is separate from certificate setup. It does not start inspection and is never implied by installing a certificate.
I understand each inspection session needs separate consent
Recorded for the next Network VPN start; inspection still waits for CA presence and selected apps.
Optional review only. Certificate setup never counts as session consent.

Start Local VPN monitoring on the Network screen after selecting apps. The route intercepts only known TCP/443 flows, keeps upstream HTTPS hostname/system trust checks, and fails selected flows closed on no-SNI, non-HTTP, pinning, or trust rejection.
Session state: not active. Start Local VPN monitoring on the Network screen; Stop remains visible while active.
TLS inspection active — selected-app scope only. Plaintext is transient and cleanup is in progress on Stop.
Stop inspection and clear transient state
Separate Android certificate setup

If you continue, APK Sentinel creates a per-install, non-exportable key in Android Keystore and opens Android\'s certificate installer. You choose whether to continue there. This does not bypass pinning, does not prove an app will trust the certificate, and does not start traffic inspection.
I understand the Android certificate setup
I want to open Android\'s certificate installer now. I understand setup is separate from inspection consent.
Read and accept the setup disclosure before opening Android\'s installer.
Open Android certificate installer
Export public CA certificate (not installed)
The app could not prepare a local certificate. Android\'s installer was not opened.
Returned from Android\'s installer. Android did not provide a generally verifiable installed/trusted result, so inspection remains off.
Public CA certificate exported. Export does not install it or prove target-app trust; use Android Settings if you are authorized to install it.
The public CA certificate could not be written to the selected document.
Certificate export cancelled. No certificate was installed.
Checking app-owned certificate setup…
No app-owned inspection certificate is prepared
Certificate installation verified
Certificate is not installed
Certificate installation status is unknown
Android has no general public API to prove a user certificate is installed and trusted by every target app. Unknown blocks every inspection session.

CA_STORE_PRESENT means only that this exact public certificate was found in AndroidCAStore. It does not mean the selected app trusts it, and pinning or app-specific policy can still reject the connection.
Android CA-store presence
Certificate fingerprint
The private key is non-exportable and stays in Android Keystore. APK Sentinel does not store certificate or key bytes.
Remove any Android-installed certificate yourself
Erasing app data removes the app-owned Keystore key, but cannot automatically remove a user certificate already added in Android Settings.
1. Stop Local VPN inspection first.
2. Open Android Security Settings and search for User credentials or Trusted credentials.
3. Find the APK Sentinel local inspection certificate and remove it in Android\'s confirmation screen.
4. Return here. If Android cannot provide a verifiable result, the status remains Unknown.
Open Android Security Settings
Android Security Settings opened. Use Android\'s own certificate-removal flow.
Android Security Settings could not be opened. Search Android Settings for User credentials or Trusted credentials.

If you opened Android\'s certificate installer, erasing local data removes only the app-owned key. A certificate you added in Android Settings may remain until you remove it there; use Network › TLS inspection for the removal steps.
Keep the decrypted session

Holds the readable content of the HTTPS sessions this app decrypted, so you can save it. This is the most revealing data the app can hold: it can include messages, search terms and page content. It stays in memory, is bounded, and is erased when you turn it off or leave the app.
Holding %1$d piece(s), %2$d bytes.
Nothing decrypted yet.
Save decrypted session
Erase now
Decrypted session saved. Treat that file as sensitive.
The decrypted session could not be saved.
Save cancelled.
Decrypted session erased from memory.
This is the readable content only. It is not a packet capture and cannot be replayed.
Save the keys that unlock this capture

Records the encryption keys for the apps you selected, and writes them into the capture file itself so Wireshark can read the traffic when you open it. Anyone who has both the capture and these keys can read that traffic.
Keys are added to a capture while it is running. Start Local VPN monitoring and a raw capture on the Network screen before the traffic you want to read.
No keys recorded yet. They appear as the selected apps make new connections.
%1$d key entries recorded
%1$d entries were not recorded because the limit was reached. Traffic after that point will not decrypt.

Erase recorded keys

The certificate is not confirmed installed, so apps may refuse it and nothing will be decrypted. Set it up below first.
